limitations: This is a four-turn checkpoint with two executed frozen cases, not a completed longitudinal evaluation or product acceptance.
Current-input grounding and same-conversation continuity do not isolate long-term database recall from recent context.
Delayed project return, schedule and folder corrections, two-Alex separation, guest-preference scoping and new completion-versus-delivery cases remain unexecuted.
The personal-memory return, cue assistance and uncommunicated photo location have not been tested; no unknown-location success is claimed.
Access aging, real model-callback change, identical-state cue experiments and human field use are not assessed.
Supported candidates can still be rejected, and literal fragmentation remains. Preserving literals does not establish a satisfactory semantic consolidation outcome.
Independent source review and model judgments are fallible; successful execution alone does not establish semantic truth.
Historical failed campaigns and the preceding paired diagnostic remain separate evidence; this checkpoint gives them no retroactive pass.

publication_review.episode_evidence_scope: One accepted episode is present in the actual publication result at journal event 68; memory-only snapshots do not independently enumerate episode rows.

scope: A reviewed historical checkpoint after the first two sessions and four delivered turns. This file does not describe the current endpoint or completion of the continuing campaign.

whole_answer_review.scope: All four complete delivered answers, judged against each actual received prefix; source text, content hashes, roles and settled delivery states were checked.

supplemental_practical_fit.detail: Two provisional slots avoid known class nights, but 45/75 minutes and completing a 1,800-word story in about two hours are ambitious. The frozen case supplies no hard duration cap.
A bounded first writing task preserves the known premise. The optional three-session plan expands the earlier two-slot aim and is not an agreed schedule.
Drafts a low-pressure access-list request without claiming to send it or adding unrelated memories.
The entire answer is shorter because it offers one draft instead of three. Its message text is longer than the earlier casual option, so literal shortening is not fully met.
